> [!WARNING]
> **Experimental compilation cache**
>
> The cache is experimental and qualified on Apple silicon Macs. Libraries are cached by the sources the compiler read, on every platform, but library caching on Linux isn't qualified yet. Build scripts, procedural macros, executables and native code are cached on Apple silicon Macs and on x86_64 and arm64 Linux with glibc, but that caching isn't qualified on Linux yet. On Linux, Tuist observes programs through the C library, so a dynamically linked program that bypasses it with raw system calls can read files Tuist doesn't see. Because shells and other programs a build script or link starts can read any environment variable unseen, those runs are keyed by the whole environment and reuse only where it matches. Cache keys replace checkout and toolchain paths with placeholders, so reuse works for checkouts at different paths on the same machine, not across machines.
